channel.title: Justin Valentine
channel.description: Robots and the tools around them, by Justin Valentine.

item.title: A test suite for the haptic wrist
item.description: I put all three joints of the final haptic wrist through bench tests for friction, inertia, bandwidth, large-signal tracking, Z-width and virtual walls, then compared it with the WHAM prototype.

item.title: Sisyphus, a bike trainer app for the Mac
item.description: My Mac app for running a smart trainer in ERG mode from a small overlay that floats over full-screen video.

item.title: A haptic lightsaber game
item.description: Sword fighting on a WAM with the haptic wrist, where clashing blades push back harder near the hilt than near the tip, played at Barrett’s booth at IROS 2026.

item.title: Teaching the Hopper Where to Put Its Foot
item.description: In simulation, I replaced the hopper's tail with a corner-balanced wheel triad, placed its foot by inverting a measured one-hop return map, and softened its landings.

item.title: The Alberta wrist
item.description: The last haptic wrist in the series, designed at Barrett Technology in 2026: from a cardboard model in May to machined parts and Barrett’s booth at IROS in September.

item.title: A Variable-Pitch Hopper
item.description: I'm building a one-legged hopper around a screw cam whose groove sets the gear ratio, plus the control board that runs it.

item.title: Getting this site off the ground
item.description: Why I keep this site as plain static pages.

item.title: Building the WHAM wrist
item.description: My biggest machining project so far: a two-joint, cable-driven haptic wrist for the WAM leader, with a thumb joystick for the follower’s last joint.

item.title: A direct-drive end-effector wrist
item.description: A 3D-printed, directly driven leader wrist for the WAM that the operator holds like an end effector, with nothing strapped to the arm; I demoed it at RISEx 2025.

item.title: The coaxial semi-differential wrist
item.description: A four-joint, cable-driven leader wrist for the WAM, with two drives stacked as rings around the forearm and a fourth motor that turns the whole wrist.

item.title: Drawing sketches with guided flow matching
item.description: A course project that generated sketches point by point with flow matching and classifier-free guidance, then had a Barrett WAM draw them on a whiteboard that presses back.

item.title: Writing DECtalk songs with an RNN
item.description: A character-level LSTM, trained on 1,085 DECtalk song files, that writes new songs for the old speech synthesizer to sing.

item.title: HAL, a quadruped with an actuated spine
item.description: A quadruped like Solo 8 but with a motorized spine, meant to backflip: the figure-skater physics behind it, a year of building, and HAL Gym for training the flip.

item.title: A simple direct-drive gimbal wrist
item.description: A directly driven gimbal wrist for the WAM, built to test whether strapping the arm to an operator’s forearm could work as an approximate exoskeleton.

item.title: A haptic mobile manipulator
item.description: A 7‑DOF WAM on a Clearpath Husky, teleoperated with force feedback from a second WAM. I designed the base and set up the sensors and ROS; we’re IDEaS finalists.

item.title: A spherical wrist after the Agile Eye
item.description: A three-motor spherical parallel mechanism I tried as a haptic wrist, and why its Jacobian is the identity matrix at the home pose.

item.title: A 360° camera from six $20 action cameras
item.description: My CMPUT 428 project with Justin Rozeboom: six cheap action cameras on an iRobot Create 2, stitched into cylindrical panoramas, plus a first try at structure from motion.

item.title: Tiling the hyperbolic plane
item.description: A Python program that draws regular hyperbolic tilings in the Poincaré disk by reflecting one polygon across its own edges, over and over.

item.title: A painting robot
item.description: My CMPUT 312 final project with Yash Bhandari: a six-servo arm from AliExpress on a wooden stand that paints SVG files onto a slanted canvas with a brush.

item.title: Localizing a Create 2 with two lasers
item.description: My idea for locating a robot in a room from two laser ranges to wall markers, worked out in pygame, plus Python to drive an iRobot Create 2.

item.title: Go on a sphere
item.description: Go on a board with no edges or corners, started during a differential geometry course with a latitude–longitude grid drawn through a stereographic projection in OpenGL.

item.title: A Rubik’s Cube solver
item.description: A Python cube simulator for any size, a beginner’s-method solver for the 3×3, and a half-finished OpenCV webcam scanner.
